test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Mid-Range Full Test - 01
subject: general
question:
**Directions:** In each of these questions, there are given three statements followed by four conclusions. You have to take the given statements as true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Decide which of the conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts.

**Statements:** Some leaves are fruits All branches are fruits. Some roots are branches.

**Conclusions: **

I. Some roots are fruits.

II. Some branches are leaves.

III. No leaf is branch.

IV. Some leaves are roots.

options.text: Either II or III and I follow
Only either II or III follows
Only I or IV and III follow

solution:
Statement:

Some leaves are fruits

All branches are fruits.

Some roots are branches.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/169570bc6fe0c3fb7cd68c7cb52d5b8e54ee77b93ad28ad3eea575b3016d6863.png] 

Conclusions:

**I. Some roots are fruits.**→ True (Because 'Some roots are branches' and 'All branches are fruits.', so 'some roots are fruit' is true.)

**II. Some branches are leaves**. → False (Because 'Some leaves are fruits' and 'All branches are fruits.', so it is possible but not definite)

**III. No leaf is branch.** → False (Because 'Some leaves are fruits' and 'All branches are fruits.', so it is possible but not definite)

**IV. Some leaves are roots.** → False (Because there is no direct relation between 'leaves' and 'roots', so it is possible but not definite)

Conclusion II and III form a complementary pair and both of them are false. Thus, this is the case of either and or.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Either II or III and I follow**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

Conditions of "Either nd or" Case 

 
• The conclusions should have a complementary pair.
 
• Both conclusions should be false.
 
• The conclusion should be in 'Some and No' form or 'All and Some not'.
